newsitem.title: USA: Lone Star Industries inventories fall.
newsitem.headline: Lone Star Industries inventories fall.

text.p: Lone Star Industries, a cement and ready mix concrete company, said increased sales pulled down cement inventory levels in the past 12 months.

Although the lower inventories (approximately 160,000 tons below last year's inventory) might result in lower shipments during the second half of 1997, compared to the same time last year, the company said it still expects the current year to be a good one.

The company said construction aggregates sales during the second quarter of 1997 were $13.5 million, comparable to sales during the same time last year. However, gross profits were reduced by 40 percent to $2.5 million.

Lone Star said in its second quarter earnings report that a decline in its construction aggregates operations reflects lower average sales prices due to customer and product mix and higher distribution costs.

In its ready-mix concrete business, the company said in a statement, the sale of its central Illinois facility and other operations during the first quarter of 1997 and lower shipments from the Memphis, Tenn. operation because of bad weather cut that division's sales by 62 percent in the second quarter.
